nodeProps.handlerPlaceholderToolCall:
-- data arrives through input:
-- input.result      - tool result text
-- input.is_error    - whether it failed (true/false)
-- input.error       - error message (only on failure)
-- input.progress    - full progress array
-- input.done        - end-of-stream marker (true)
--
-- this script also runs for each progress item as it arrives:
-- input.progress     - that progress item as an object
-- input.progress_raw - that progress item as raw JSON
--
-- the fixed output variables result / progress / error are always written by the node,
-- returning those names from the script is ignored. The script only handles custom output variables:
-- return { myVar = value }  (strings are appended, other types overwrite)
nodeProps.handlerPlaceholderHttp:
-- response data arrives through input:
-- input.mode     - "complete" | "sse_stream"
-- input.status   - HTTP status code
-- input.headers  - response headers (object)
-- input.body     - response body
-- input.event    - SSE event object {id, event, data}
-- input.done     - stream-closed marker (true/false)
--
-- the fixed output variables mode / status / headers / body / sse_events / stream_finished
-- are written by the node; do not set them in the script. The script only writes custom output variables:
-- return { text = input.body }   (strings are appended, other types overwrite)
nodeProps.handlerPlaceholderLlmSse:
-- input.mode / input.content / input.reasoning_content / input.tool_calls / input.done
-- the fixed variables content / reasoning_content / tool_calls are accumulated by the node, do not write them
-- called once per frame and stateless: input.content is that frame's delta
-- the script only writes custom output variables: strings are appended, other types overwrite
return { answer = input.content }
nodeProps.handlerPlaceholderLlmComplete:
-- input.mode / input.content / input.reasoning_content / input.tool_calls / input.done
-- the fixed variables content / reasoning_content / tool_calls are written by the node, do not write them
-- the script only writes custom output variables: strings are appended, other types overwrite
return { answer = input.content }
nodeProps.handlerScriptDefault:
-- write the response handling script here
return { content = input.content }

exit.p1: The terminate node exits the whole flow immediately.
exit.p2: When the flow reaches this node, the whole flow stops and no later node runs.
exit.p3: This node also runs inside a function node, but mind the difference from the return node.

return.p1: The return node exits the current function.
return.p2: When the flow reaches this node, it leaves the current function and resumes at the caller.
return.p3: This node can only be created inside a function node.

break.p2: When the flow reaches this node, it exits the innermost loop immediately and skips the remaining iterations.

continue.p2: When the flow reaches this node, it skips the remaining steps of the current iteration and moves to the next one.

variables.flowIntro: Flow variables store data while the flow runs and can be read or written by any node.
variables.globalIntro1: Global variables are shared by every flow, agent and skill of this tenant. They are read-only here; maintain them in Settings → Global variables.
variables.globalIntro2: To use one, pick it as the source of a node input variable and reference that input variable in templates.
variables.noGlobalVars: No global variables yet (create them in Settings → Global variables)
variables.envIntro1: Environment variables hold runtime settings of the flow: strings, numbers and secrets.
variables.envIntro2: Tenant-wide settings (addresses, accounts, secrets) do not live here: pick Global variables as the source of a node input variable and reference it in templates.
variables.secretPlaceholderSet: Already set; leave empty to keep it
variables.secretHint: A value is set but never shown; leaving the field empty keeps it. To clear it, delete and recreate the variable.
